text:
Alex: Heads-up — we need to finalize the exporters + aggregation + retention plan for the new runtime dashboards (routing/quotas/rollouts metrics). Can we use this thread to lock owners and a timeline?

Maria: +1. Product wants p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/s, error_rate_per_1k, capacity_utilization by pool. Dashboards will query aggregated series; real-time panels need ~15s refresh.

Sanjay: For infra, avoid keeping raw high-cardinality metrics >30d. Proposal: raw Prometheus samples -> Thanos (object store) for 30d, rollups -> ClickHouse for 2yr aggregates. Keeps query cost down.

Jia: Agree on storage split. Need to know what labels we must keep for aggregation. Current runtime exporter only scrapes {service, model}. We need: deployment_id, pool, region, routing_policy, customer_tier.

Alex: Adding routing_policy label is critical for console breakdown. Can we add those to the exporter without too much perf hit?

Sanjay: Adding 3 low-card labels is okay if we limit cardinality values. routing_policy should be enums (latency|cost|fallback), customer_tier (free|pro|enterprise). That's safe.

Priya: SRE concern: increasing label cardinality can spike TSDB memory during scrapes. Suggest enforcing a whitelist on deployment_id for prod clusters only, and aggregate deployment_id -> deployment_bucket for dashboards to reduce cardinality.

Jia: For aggregation jobs we can group_by(bucket(deployment_id, 1000)) or use modulo hash to keep consistent buckets. I'll prototype a ClickHouse rollup that bins deployments.

Tom: Quick ask from Product: we need backfill for the last 90 days of latency for the rollout page so we can do trend comparisons. Is that feasible?

Sanjay: Backfill is feasible but will be I/O heavy. If we backfill raw samples from object store into ClickHouse aggregates, estimate: ~2TB read + heavy CPU for windowed aggregations. Needs a maintenance window and cost estimate.

Maria: Can we do incremental backfill (oldest -> newest) and pause during business hours? Product only needs metric-level trends, not per-deployment granularity for older data.

Alex: Proposal: backfill 90d of rolled-up aggregates (not raw high-card) into ClickHouse. Raw samples remain in Thanos for 30d. Aggregated metrics: 1m, 5m, 1h windows stored for 2yr. Agree?

Priya: I can accept that. Add rate-limiting on backfill jobs and a circuit-breaker if ClickHouse queue > 80% capacity. Also add an alert to eng-sre for backfill failures.

Jia: Implementation plan: 1) Add labels to runtime exporter (deployment_bucket, routing_policy, customer_tier). 2) Update OTEL collector config to forward to Prometheus/Thanos. 3) Run transform jobs that compute 1m/5m/1h aggregates into ClickHouse. 4) Backfill 90d (aggregate-only) with throttling. I'll own steps 2-4.

Sanjay: I'll own exporter changes with Alex — need PRs for envoy filters and runtime lib updates. Expect 2-week window for rollout and canary on dedicated pools.

Maria: Dashboard work: I'll create new panels and temp dashboards. Need sample queries from Jia's prototype. ETA for dashboards once data in ClickHouse: 3 business days.

Tom: On metrics selection — product baseline: p99 latency, request_rate, error_rate_per_1k, tokens_out_per_minute, autoscale_events, per-pool_throughput. Keep that list as the baseline.

Alex: Decision summary: raw samples -> Thanos (30d). Aggregated (1m/5m/1h) -> ClickHouse (2yr). Exporter labels: deployment_bucket, routing_policy, customer_tier. Backfill 90d of aggregates only. Owners: Jia (pipeline + backfill), Sanjay (exporter), Alex (coord + rollout), Maria (dashboards), Priya (sre guardrails). Timeline: exporter PRs by EOW, collector rollout week after, backfill scheduled next week (off-peak), dashboards live within 2 weeks.

OpsBot: backfill-job-queue: started_backfill(run_id=7821) — estimated completion 18h; throttle=20%; status=queued

Priya: Please add an alert: clickhouse.backfill.job.failures >=1 -> pager to eng-sre, and a runbook with steps to abort backfill.

Jia: Will add alert + runbook. Also will include sample ClickHouse query for p99 latency (will paste into the dashboard PR).

Sanjay: One more note — update our SDK/platform docs about the new labels and opt-in for customers who run self-hosted exporters.

Maria: Noted. I'll add cross-link in dashboard docs.

Alex: Thanks everyone — I'll follow up with a small GH issue that lists the concrete tasks and owners. Ping me if anything blocks.

Sanjay: :thumbsup:

Tom: Thanks — excited to see the rollout metrics in the console.

End of thread.
